operating_brief.existing_holdings_meaning: No sector portfolio exists within this new-money task; null is not unknown actual institutional holdings.

evidence_items.statement: This is a hypothetical research assignment to recommend a new US equity-sector sleeve, not to impersonate any institution or infer its private mandate.
Use a 2026-07-17 decision reference and only supplied observations and public releases before that date. This is a documentary retrospective case, not a point-in-time trading replay.
The allocation judgment horizon is 12 months. This is not a 12-month realized-return test. Document view dates and horizons remain those of their respective sources.

Propose a reasoned allocation intended for capital appreciation over the stated horizon, explaining diversification and risk-return trade-offs relative to the common sector benchmark. No required return or unique optimal allocation is specified.

The hypothetical assignment accepts equity-market loss risk and provides no capital guarantee. No numerical risk-aversion coefficient, volatility ceiling, loss budget or sector cap is supplied. Do not invent one; discuss remaining risk and uncertainty.

This is new money assigned to an equity sleeve with no existing sector holdings. Recommend target weights, not trades from current holdings. The S&P sector benchmark is only a comparison anchor and is not the starting portfolio.

Use exactly the supplied 11 GICS sector baskets, with one row for each sector including zero weights. The submitted allocation must be long-only, unlevered and fully invested: raw weights sum to one. Individual stocks, cash, bonds and derivatives are outside this sleeve task.

The deliverable is an allocation proposal for review, not a trade order or a whole-client financial plan. Transaction costs, turnover, tax optimization, withdrawals and actual client suitability are not measured. Do not invent missing client or liquidity requirements.

For this hypothetical sleeve there are no scheduled withdrawals during the judgment horizon and no separate ESG exclusion. These are declared task assumptions, not observed facts about a real institution or customer.

Use dated market observations and any institution packet currently supplied. Published outlook ratings are not binding weight constraints or target holdings. Explain justified adoption, qualification or departure and any age/horizon mismatch. Do not assume the outlook author had observed later common market releases.

market_context.role: Common factual macro context supplied from the first draft to every condition, alongside the existing eleven-sector market packet and common task brief.
information_policy: Use these dated release values as the common information set. Observation periods and publication dates are different fields.
No fact in this packet implies a prescribed sector preference or allocation. A model may draw a conditional inference but must label it as its own inference and cite the relevant evidence IDs.
The target-date context is July 2026; do not insert knowledge of later outcomes, later statistical revisions, or today's market state.
A source outlook may have been written before these releases. Treat any resulting tension as dated evidence to explain, not as evidence that the outlook's author saw subsequent information.
